topic_definitions._how_to_edit: Plain-English definitions used to score how well each paper fits a section. Edit 'about' and 'not' freely; no author or lab names are used, so ranking stays topic-based. Keyword rules in the updater remain the hard filter.
_global_not: plant biology, crops, agriculture or plant extracts
veterinary medicine, dog or livestock breeds and animal genetics
cancer treatment, tumour growth, chemotherapy and oncology outcomes
clinical neuroimaging, MRI connectivity, diagnostic prediction or epidemiology without cellular or molecular experiments
materials science, surface chemistry, explosives, sensors or engineering microscopy
herbal medicine, traditional Chinese medicine, natural product extracts or dietary supplements
dentistry, dermatology, cardiology, nephrology or liver disease
remote sensing, satellite images or environmental microbiology
hospital care, nursing, health services or medical education

focus.about: Direct studies of the JIP3 protein (MAPK8IP3): its role in axonal transport of lysosomes, endo-lysosomal maturation, kinesin and dynein motor adaptor function, MAPK8IP3 patient variants causing neurodevelopmental disorders, and closely related JIP4 mechanisms in neurons.
not: LRRK2 or Rab proteins without JIP3
JNK stress signalling in heart, kidney or cancer

neurodevelopment.about: Mechanisms of neurodevelopmental disorders and rare genetic brain diseases: intellectual disability and autism genes, patient variants, brain development, neuronal migration, axon guidance, corpus callosum and commissure formation, studied in mouse, human or iPSC neural models.
not: psychiatric questionnaires or clinical service studies

organelle.about: Cell biology of lysosomes and endosomes: lysosome biogenesis, positioning, acidification, membrane damage and repair, lysophagy, TFEB, lysosomal storage disorders, and endo-lysosomal maturation, especially in neurons and glia.
not: lysosomes in liver, kidney or skin disease

trafficking.about: Intracellular membrane trafficking and organelle transport: retromer, retriever, WASH, CCC/Commander, ESCRT, HOPS/CORVET, exocyst, Rab GTPase-controlled sorting, and kinesin/dynein-driven axonal transport of organelles in neurons.

cytoskeleton.about: Neuronal cytoskeleton: microtubules, actin, neurofilaments, dynein, dynactin, kinesins and myosins in axons, dendrites, growth cones, the axon initial segment, neuronal polarity and organelle transport.
not: epithelial or cancer cell migration without neurons

ipsc.about: Human induced pluripotent stem cell neural models: iPSC-derived neurons, microglia, astrocytes, motor neurons and brain organoids used to study neurological disease mechanisms, patient variants and isogenic controls.
not: iPSC-derived heart, liver or blood cells

omics.about: Proteomics, phosphoproteomics, interactomics, lipidomics, single-cell, single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics, and CRISPR screens that answer questions about neurons, glia, lysosomes, trafficking or neurodegeneration, or provide reusable brain datasets.

imaging.about: Microscopy and imaging of cells and neurons: live-cell imaging, super-resolution (STED, STORM, expansion), light-sheet, two-photon, electron microscopy and cryo-ET, and new imaging methods or probes for organelles, synapses and axonal transport.
not: medical radiology, MRI or CT scans

analysis-tools.about: Software tools, plugins and pipelines for analysing biological microscopy and cell data: image segmentation, particle and cell tracking, kymograph analysis, neurite tracing, Sholl analysis, colocalization, puncta counting, napari, Fiji/ImageJ, CellProfiler, QuPath, and open-source bioimage analysis.
not: clinical documentation or health records software

signaling.about: Mechanisms of cAMP, EPAC, PKA and AKAP signalling; AKT, PI3K and mTOR; Rab and Rho family small GTPases (RhoA, Rac1, Cdc42); TBK1, STING, TMEM55B, RILPL1, CC2D1A and related regulators in neurons, lysosomes and membrane trafficking.
not: a drug or compound alleviating disease through a pathway

extracellular.about: Extracellular vesicles, exosomes and microvesicles released by neurons, microglia and astrocytes; lysosomal exocytosis, secretory lysosomes, secretory autophagy and unconventional protein secretion mechanisms.

neurodegeneration.about: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of Parkinson's disease, LRRK2, ALS/FTD, Alzheimer's disease and related neurodegeneration involving lysosomes, trafficking, axonal transport, glia, cytoskeleton, small GTPases or ferroptosis.
not: clinical progression scales or diagnostic codes
